title: The Price of a Moon-Finch
story: Under the paper lanterns of the Night Market, Brasselwick the Cage Hawker sells songbirds that were never his to sell. A single moon-finch sits in a brass cage, singing a tune that makes the whole market sad. Mr 6 counts his ember coins and his wits, and decides the wits will matter more.
question: The moon-finch is marked at 240 ember coins. Brasselwick adds a 25% "feather tax" to that price, but Mr 6 unrolls the Realm Charter of Freed Songbirds, which takes 40% off the taxed total. How many ember coins does Mr 6 actually pay?
solution: The feather tax adds 240 × 0.25 = 60, so the taxed price is 240 + 60 = 300 ember coins.
The charter takes 40% off that, which is 300 × 0.40 = 120 coins off, leaving 300 - 120 = 180.
praise: Working with the percents was the right plan — the trick is doing them in order, tax first and then the charter's discount on the NEW total.
hint: Do the tax before the discount: find the taxed price first, then take 40% off that number (not off 240).
victory: Brasselwick squints at the charter, squints at the math, and hands over the cage with a defeated little bow. The moon-finch sings one perfect note and the entire market finally stops feeling sad.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight holding an unrolled glowing charter before a weaselly lantern-lit market hawker surrounded by brass birdcages, warm amber light and curious shoppers crowding in.
